reasons: The file is over 2400 lines and mixes many screens, which makes changes hard to verify.
No test evidence is visible in the packet.
Some helpers handle edge cases well, such as spreadsheet-safe values and missing dates.

terms.meaning: A library for building screens from reusable pieces called components.
A reusable piece of screen that takes inputs and draws part of the page.
Information a screen remembers while it runs, such as which project is selected.
An input passed from one component to another.
Comma-separated values, a plain text format that spreadsheet programs open.
TypeScript with HTML-like markup, the file type used for React screens.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Imports for the main screens
sections.what: Brings in the screens, data loaders, 3D view parts, timeline helpers and styling that the main application needs.
sections.why: Likely reason: the root screen combines many features, so it needs a wide set of imports.
sections.watch_out: A missing or renamed import only shows up when the screen loads.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Data type imports and two constants
sections.what: Brings in the data types used across the screens and sets the length of one day in milliseconds and the number of activities per timeline page.
sections.why: Likely reason: a shared day length keeps date maths consistent, and the page size limits how much is loaded at once.
sections.watch_out: The page size affects loading speed, so changing it changes how many pages the timeline requests.

sections.name: PHASE_LABELS
sections.title: Readable phase names
sections.what: Maps each internal phase code to the label shown to the user, such as Excavation / advance or Operation readiness.
sections.why: Likely reason: users should see plain names, not internal codes.
sections.watch_out: The table must cover every phase in the backend, and a new phase must be added here too, or the build will fail.

sections.name: storyDate
sections.title: Choosing an activity date
sections.what: Picks the chosen date for an activity from the selected basis, such as planned, baseline, forecast or actual, falling back to the paired date when the first is missing. It returns a time value, or nothing if no valid date exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same activity can be viewed against different schedule versions, so the basis has to be chosen first.
sections.watch_out: An activity with no valid date is left off the timeline, so missing dates can make work disappear from view.

sections.name: downloadText
sections.title: Saving text as a download
sections.what: Turns a text string into a file and triggers a browser download, then releases the memory after one second.
sections.why: Likely reason: exports such as spreadsheets and reports are created in the browser, so no server copy is needed.
sections.watch_out: Some browsers or settings may block a download that is started without a direct user click.

sections.name: csvValue
sections.title: Spreadsheet-safe values
sections.what: Formats one value for a CSV file: converts it to text, wraps it in quotes, doubles any inner quotes, and adds an apostrophe before values that a spreadsheet could read as a formula.
sections.why: Likely reason: schedule text can contain characters that spreadsheets treat as formulas, which can run commands, so the apostrophe guards against this.
sections.watch_out: This protects against spreadsheet formula injection; removing the apostrophe step would reopen that risk.

sections.name: AccuracyCard
sections.title: Accuracy card
sections.what: Shows one accuracy measure as a percentage ring with the matching numerator and denominator counts beneath it.
sections.why: Likely reason: users need a quick visual summary of how much of the data matched.
sections.watch_out: When the denominator is zero the card shows zero percent, which can look like a failure rather than an absence of data.

sections.name: ProjectChooser (part 1)
sections.title: Project chooser, part one
sections.what: Shows the first screen after an upload: the source name, encoding, record count and project count, with buttons for the programme view and the combined 3D view. Both buttons are disabled while generation runs.
sections.why: Likely reason: projects must be chosen before generation, and disabling the buttons prevents a second run from starting.
sections.watch_out: The disabled state depends on the generating flag, so if that flag gets stuck the user cannot open either view.

sections.name: ProjectChooser (part 2)
sections.title: Project cards and ingestion warnings
sections.what: Shows one card per project in the schedule, with its activity count, relationship count and date window. Cards for projects over the activity limit are greyed out and labelled as programme mode only. A collapsible list shows up to 100 import warnings.
sections.why: Likely reason: the 3D model cannot be built for very large projects, so the card explains the limit instead of letting the user try.
sections.watch_out: The limit comes from MAX_PROJECT_MODEL_ACTIVITIES, so changing that value changes which cards are disabled.

sections.name: ProjectChooser (part 3)
sections.title: Empty line after project chooser
sections.what: This range contains only a blank line. It does not add any screen content or behaviour.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: MAPPING_FIELDS
sections.title: Column names for the mapping form
sections.what: A fixed list of the fields the app needs from a schedule file, each paired with the label shown to the user. Required fields are marked with an asterisk, and planned finish or duration is marked with a dagger because one of the two is needed.
sections.why: Lets the user tell the app which spreadsheet column holds which schedule detail when the file headers are unclear.
sections.watch_out: The field keys here must match the names the backend expects, or the mapping will be silently ignored.

sections.name: ReviewGate
sections.title: Review screen before opening the model
sections.what: Shows the project name, the guessed facility type, its confidence, and the list of open review items. The user can accept the conservative model and open the viewer, or start again.
sections.why: Makes the user see the uncertainty before the 3D model is shown. The on-screen text says accepting does not raise confidence or invent evidence.
sections.watch_out: The review list is only as complete as the backend's review queue. Items missing from that queue will not appear here.

sections.name: ProgrammeView (part 1)
sections.title: Programme view setup and playback state
sections.what: Sets up the multi-project programme screen. It keeps track of whether playback is running, the current date on the timeline, and the activities for the chosen project filter, sorted by date.
sections.why: Lets one screen show many projects on one timeline, with a filter to show just one project.
sections.watch_out: The timeline start and end come from the schedule origin and finish dates, so missing dates produce a timeline starting at zero.

sections.name: ProgrammeView: for
sections.title: Finding the current activity and animating time
sections.what: Finds the latest activity that has started by the current date, which drives the subtitle. When playing, it moves the date forward by about 90 days each second and stops at the end of the timeline.
sections.why: Likely reason: the programme screen shows what is happening at a chosen date, and playback gives a moving view of the schedule.
sections.watch_out: The activity search assumes activities are sorted by date. Unsorted data will show the wrong current activity.

sections.name: ProgrammeView (part 3)
sections.title: Programme header and project filter
sections.what: Shows the programme title, totals, and the number of cross-project links at the top. Offers a dropdown to filter by project, which resets the date and asks for the first page of data. It also has the buttons to open the 3D programme, go back, and play or pause.
sections.why: Changing the filter needs a fresh data load, so the screen resets the date and page to match the new choice.
sections.watch_out: The reset date for a single project comes from that project's planned start, so a project with no start date jumps to a blank date.

sections.name: ProgrammeView (part 4)
sections.title: Timeline navigation buttons
sections.what: Buttons that jump the timeline to the start, the end, the previous or next activity date, and show the current date.
sections.why: Gives the user step-by-step control over the timeline, not just smooth playback.
sections.watch_out: The previous and next buttons rely on the helper adjacentEvent, which is not defined in the code shown here, so its exact behaviour cannot be confirmed.

sections.name: ProgrammeView (part 5)
sections.title: Date slider and current activity subtitle
sections.what: A slider that moves the timeline date, a hidden status message for screen readers, and a subtitle that names the activity active at that date with its code and project. If nothing has started, the subtitle says so. The list of project lanes begins here.
sections.why: The slider gives direct date control, and the subtitle tells the user what they are looking at. The screen-reader text helps users who cannot see the screen.
sections.watch_out: Changing the slider stops playback, so a user who drags the slider while playing will see playback stop.

sections.name: ProgrammeView (part 6)
sections.title: Project lanes, cross-project links and footer
sections.what: Draws one card per project showing its fidelity level, dates and layout reason, with a button to open that project's 3D model. Below it, lists each link that crosses project boundaries with both project and activity identities. The footer shows the source file fingerprint and the list of limitations.
sections.why: Keeps each project's identity separate, so links between projects are shown without merging the projects into one.
sections.watch_out: The source fingerprint in the footer is the only proof of which file the data came from, so it should match the file the user thinks they loaded.

sections.name: MappingWizard (part 1)
sections.title: Column mapping form setup
sections.what: Starts the column mapping screen. It fills the form with the column choices the backend guessed, then shows one dropdown per schedule field, each listing the file's column headers.
sections.why: Lets the user correct the backend's guesses before the file is read again.
sections.watch_out: Column numbers are stored as text in the form and converted to numbers on submit, so a bad conversion would send a wrong column.

sections.name: MappingWizard (part 2)
sections.title: Apply mapping button and error message
sections.what: The submit button sends the chosen column numbers to the backend and reads the file again. While that runs, the button shows a busy message and cannot be clicked. Any error from the backend appears in a red alert box.
sections.why: Stops the user from submitting twice while the file is being reprocessed, and shows any problem clearly.
sections.watch_out: Empty dropdown choices are removed before sending, so a required field left blank fails only when the backend checks it.

sections.name: Inspector, WorkspacePanel (part 1)
sections.title: Inspector setup and empty state
sections.what: The side panel that explains a selected 3D component. When nothing is selected, it shows a short hint and, if a site plan exists, the plan's size and its source file. When something is selected, it works out how that component stands on the chosen timeline basis, such as planned or forecast.
sections.why: The inspector explains why each object exists and when it appears, so the user can check the model rather than trust it.
sections.watch_out: The helpers componentState, timelineBounds and the basis date lookups are not defined in this file, so their rules are not confirmed here.

sections.name: Inspector, WorkspacePanel (part 2)
sections.title: Component facts in the inspector
sections.what: Shows the selected component's ID, its label, a confidence badge coloured high, medium or low, its phase, facility area, class, material, quantity, dates for the chosen basis, status rule and duration.
sections.why: Gives the user the key facts about one object in a single list.
sections.watch_out: Confidence colours change at 80 and 60 percent, so a change to those thresholds changes the colours without changing any data.

sections.name: Inspector, WorkspacePanel (part 3)
sections.title: Evidence and provenance sections
sections.what: Lists the words that led to the classification, then shows separate blocks for position, timing, material and geometry provenance. Each block shows whether the data was measured, derived or assumed, with the reason and source. The geometry block also lists shape and size.
sections.why: Makes clear where each fact came from, so the user does not mistake a guess for a survey.
sections.watch_out: Each provenance block only appears if its data exists, so a missing block does not mean the value is known.

sections.name: Inspector, WorkspacePanel (part 4)
sections.title: Layout, scores and linked records
sections.what: Shows the position and rotation of the component, the layout reason, the score breakdown for each possible class, the links to other structures, and collapsible lists of activity IDs and source fact IDs. It also includes a part inspector for the component.
sections.why: Lets the user trace any object back to the schedule activities and source facts that produced it.
sections.watch_out: The part inspector is keyed on the component ID, so it resets when the selection changes.

sections.name: WORKSPACE_DOCK
sections.title: Panel names for the workspace dock
sections.what: The list of panels that can be opened from the bottom dock, each with the label the user sees, such as Filters, Labels, Timeline and Captions.
sections.why: Gives one place to define which panels exist and what they are called.
sections.watch_out: Adding a panel here does nothing until it is also given a default setting and a floating panel in the viewer.

sections.name: DEFAULT_PANELS
sections.title: Default panel visibility and top spacing
sections.what: Sets which panels start open. Layers, checklist, timeline, lifecycle and captions start open, while the others start closed. It also reserves 44 pixels at the top of the screen for the dock.
sections.why: Chooses a sensible first view, so the screen is not crowded when the model first opens.
sections.watch_out: The 44 pixel space must match the dock height in the styles, or floating panels will overlap the dock.

sections.name: Viewer (part 1)
sections.title: Viewer main state and model setup
sections.what: Sets up the 3D viewer. It stores the model, the label settings, the timeline basis, the current date, playback speed, the set of visible phases, and the display options such as shadows, cutaway and ground.
sections.why: Holds all the viewer's settings in one place, so the screen can change when the user adjusts a control.
sections.watch_out: The saved view key is built from a hash of the whole model. It is a convenience for remembering settings, not a check that the data is correct.

sections.name: Viewer (part 2)
sections.title: Viewer selection, filter and tour state
sections.what: Holds the current selection, the active tab, the search text, the discipline, area, WBS and confidence filters, the hidden items, the chosen story, the chosen guided tour and the explanation level. Some values are restored from the last saved view when it is valid.
sections.why: Lets the user return to the same view after reloading, and keeps every filter in one place.
sections.watch_out: Restored values are checked against the model before use, so a stale saved view falls back to defaults instead of breaking.

sections.name: Viewer: if
sections.title: Building the guided tour list
sections.what: Builds the ordered list of stops for the chosen guided tour. A tour can use activity stories or individual components. Each stop is matched to a story that changed that component.
sections.why: Turns the tour choice into a clear sequence the user can step through.
sections.watch_out: Components with no matching story are dropped from the tour without any warning to the user.

sections.name: Viewer (part 4)
sections.title: Jumping to stories, tour stops and playlists
sections.what: Moves the timeline and the camera to a chosen activity story, moves through the tour, and starts a playlist from its first stop. Jumping to a story stops playback unless playback is already in progress.
sections.why: Makes it easy to go from an activity to what it changes in the model.
sections.watch_out: The camera focus is delayed by one animation frame, so the target must exist when that frame runs.

sections.name: Viewer (part 5)
sections.title: Selection and filtered set of components
sections.what: Handles picking a component, finds the selected component and its structure, and builds the lists used by the filters. It also computes which components pass every active filter, which is the set the viewer draws.
sections.why: Keeps one definition of what is visible, so the viewer, counts and filters always agree.
sections.watch_out: A component must pass every filter at once. Adding a filter here without adding it to the list of dependencies can leave the view out of date.

sections.name: Viewer (part 6)
sections.title: Keeping the viewer in sync
sections.what: Resets playback and the date when the timeline basis changes. Saves the viewer's settings for the current job. Opens the inspector when a component is selected. Advances the guided tour on a timer while playing. Works out the labels to show on screen and counts components in each status.
sections.why: Keeps the screen consistent as the user changes settings, and runs the tour without the user clicking each stop.
sections.watch_out: The tour timer's delay is based on the playback speed, so a change to speed changes how fast the tour moves.

sections.name: Viewer: for
sections.title: Status counts and the schedule lane
sections.what: Counts how many components are future, active, complete or unavailable on the current date. Loads a page of the schedule lane from the backend when a job exists, otherwise uses the lane stored in the model. Shows any error from loading the page.
sections.why: Gives the user a quick summary of progress, and keeps the schedule lane small by loading it page by page.
sections.watch_out: If the page fails to load, the lane is emptied, so the user sees no schedule items rather than the old ones.

sections.name: Viewer (part 8)
sections.title: Search, screenshot and downloads
sections.what: Finds structures by name, ID or evidence words. Takes a PNG screenshot of the 3D view. Downloads the full model as JSON, or the list of structures as a CSV file. The download names are built from the project name and the date.
sections.why: Lets the user search the model, save images and take the data out for other tools.
sections.watch_out: The CSV columns are written directly from the data, so the escaping done by csvValue is what keeps commas inside text from breaking the file.

sections.name: Viewer (part 9)
sections.title: Viewer header and tabs
sections.what: Shows the project name and a summary of facility, structures and components. Shows a warning banner when the model is marked as an unreleased package. Provides four tabs: model, schedule, evidence and review, with the review count shown. Also has the header buttons for the programme, screenshot, export and a new project.
sections.why: Gives the user a clear starting point and shows at once if the model is not yet final.
sections.watch_out: The unreleased banner appears only if a limitation text starts with the exact words used in the check, so changing that wording removes the warning.

sections.name: Viewer (part 10)
sections.title: Export menu and the specifications panel
sections.what: The export menu offers offline HTML, an audit pack, an IFC file, an ALICE contract, and the model JSON and structure CSV. The backend downloads only appear once a job exists. Also starts the floating panel for equipment specifications, which lets the user change the model through the parametric editor.
sections.why: Lets the user export the model in the formats other tools expect.
sections.watch_out: Backend export links are shown only when a job exists, so a model loaded offline has only the local downloads.

sections.name: Viewer (part 11)
sections.title: Labels panel controls
sections.what: Controls the labels on the 3D model. The user chooses when labels show, which details each label shows, and can add or remove a label on the selected component. Hidden labels can be restored, and added labels can be cleared. A checkbox adds area labels.
sections.why: Lets the user decide which parts of the model are labelled, so the screen is not crowded.
sections.watch_out: The label choices are kept separately from the hidden and added sets, so clearing one set does not change the other.

sections.name: Viewer (part 12)
sections.title: View controls: search, tours and story search
sections.what: The view controls panel starts here. It has the structure search with a result list, a guided tour selector with previous and next buttons showing the position in the tour, and a search that jumps to an activity story.
sections.why: Gives the user several ways to find something in the model and follow the guided tour.
sections.watch_out: The tour buttons are disabled when there are no stops, so an empty playlist shows the controls but cannot be used.

sections.name: Viewer (part 13)
sections.title: Story results, voice and camera presets
sections.what: Shows the list of matching activity stories, a checkbox that turns on spoken narration in the browser, and buttons that move the camera to preset views such as overview, top, side and below ground.
sections.why: Gives the user quick ways to look at the model from set angles and to hear the story aloud.
sections.watch_out: The voice uses the browser's own speech, so it works only where the browser supports it.

sections.name: Viewer (part 14)
sections.title: Look, colour and display toggles
sections.what: Switches between engineering and realistic looks. The colour choice is disabled in realistic mode, because realistic mode always uses material colours. Also has checkboxes for future-as-blueprint, shadows, cutaway plane, ground grid, and isolating the selected component.
sections.why: Lets the user choose how the model looks and how much of it is shown at once.
sections.watch_out: The page states that status follows the supplied dates and that the geometry is not measured field progress, so the colours do not show real site progress.

sections.name: Viewer (part 15)
sections.title: Activity isolation and hiding
sections.what: Adds checkboxes to isolate the components of the current activity and to dim the other components around it. Also has buttons to hide the selected component and to show all hidden components again, with a count.
sections.why: Lets the user focus on what changes during one activity, or remove a part of the view that gets in the way.
sections.watch_out: The activity checkboxes are disabled when no activity is active, so they cannot be used on an empty timeline.

sections.name: Viewer (part 16)
sections.title: Filters and phase checkboxes
sections.what: Provides dropdowns for discipline, facility area, WBS group and minimum confidence, followed by a checkbox per physical phase. A closing note reminds the user that there is no survey or BIM claim, so every component should be checked for its source.
sections.why: Lets the user narrow the model to the parts they care about, and keeps the provenance warning visible.
sections.watch_out: Phase checkboxes come from the phases found in the model, so a phase missing from the data cannot be turned on.

sections.name: Viewer (part 17)
sections.title: Main 3D scene and subtitle header
sections.what: Draws the main 3D model of the project, along with a badge showing how confident the model is. While a scheduled event is playing, it also shows a subtitle card that starts with the activity name, the lifecycle stage and the event's position in the sequence.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the 3D scene and the explanation of the current event on one screen, so the viewer sees what changes and why.
sections.watch_out: The subtitle header depends on the selected story being present, so clearing the selection hides the card.

sections.name: Viewer (part 18)
sections.title: Subtitle text and explanation level
sections.what: Shows the plain description of the current activity and lets the user choose between beginner, construction professional, and engineering audit wording. It also lists planned, baseline, forecast and actual dates for that activity.
sections.why: Likely reason: different readers need different amounts of technical detail for the same event.
sections.watch_out: Dates are cut to their first ten characters, so any time of day is hidden from the subtitle.

sections.name: Viewer (part 19)
sections.title: Evidence trail and schedule overlay start
sections.what: Shows which source file and page supplied the activity, how its geometry, position and timing were derived, the site plan size if one exists, and the accuracy limit. This block also opens the floating overlay used for the schedule, evidence and review tabs.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes clear which facts are from the source and which are estimated, so reviewers can check them.
sections.watch_out: When no source is linked, the text reads typed source unavailable, so an empty evidence trail is possible and looks similar to a missing feature.

sections.name: Viewer (part 20)
sections.title: Schedule list page and status colours
sections.what: Shows one page of abstract activities and marks each as future, active or complete based on the chosen date basis. Previous and next page buttons move through the list.
sections.why: Likely reason: paging keeps large schedules responsive in the browser.
sections.watch_out: Status depends on the chosen date basis, so switching basis can change which rows look complete or active.

sections.name: Viewer (part 21)
sections.title: Evidence and review tabs
sections.what: The evidence tab shows the four separate accuracy scores and the top grouping candidates. The review tab lists low-confidence decisions and physical activities that have no geometric shape.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page states that accuracy is several separate measures, so one score would mislead.
sections.watch_out: Lists are cut off after 20 grouping candidates and 300 unrepresented activities, so long lists are not complete on screen.

sections.name: Viewer (part 22)
sections.title: Floating panels for inspector, layers and checklist
sections.what: Opens three movable panels. The inspector shows the selected element, element layers lets the user hide or colour element kinds, and the work checklist lists work items for the current date.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the 3D view uncluttered while giving detail when the user asks for it.
sections.watch_out: Hidden kinds and colour choices are kept only in page memory, so they appear to reset when the page reloads.

sections.name: Viewer (part 23)
sections.title: Timeline play and jump buttons
sections.what: The bottom timeline bar has Play or Pause, Start, previous and next event, End, Data date and Today buttons. Pressing Play at the end of the list starts again from the first event.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user step through schedule events one at a time or play them.
sections.watch_out: Pressing Play also turns off isolate mode, and the Data date button only appears when the model has a data date.

sections.name: Viewer (part 24)
sections.title: Date basis, playback speed and date slider
sections.what: Lets the user pick the planned, baseline, forecast or actual date set, with unavailable sets greyed out. It also sets playback speed in days per second and provides a slider for any date. Dragging the slider stops playback and clears the current selection.
sections.why: Likely reason: different date sets tell different stories, and the slider allows precise jumps.
sections.watch_out: Speed is measured in schedule days per real second, so the speed does not match real time.

sections.name: Viewer (part 25)
sections.title: Timeline status counts
sections.what: Shows how many components are complete, active, future or unavailable, how many abstract activities exist, and a note that the ground is flat rather than real terrain.
sections.why: Likely reason: explains the colour legend so the user knows what solid, ghost and blueprint mean.
sections.watch_out: Future items are hidden unless the blueprint toggle is on, so the count can differ from what is visible.

sections.name: UploadApplication
sections.title: Starting screen chooser
sections.what: Decides which screen to show: the viewer, the review gate, the programme view, the mapping wizard, the project chooser, or the upload screen. It also starts the bundled demo, which loads sample files and processes them.
sections.why: Likely reason: the order of these checks decides which screen the user sees first.
sections.watch_out: If a sample file fails to load, the demo ends and an alert shows the error.

sections.name: SavedProgrammeLanes
sections.title: Saved combined programme view
sections.what: Shows a saved combined programme and lets the user page through its activities and relationships. Building the combined 3D view repeatedly checks the job status and reloads the page when finished.
sections.why: Likely reason: building 3D runs in the background on the server, so the page keeps polling until it is done.
sections.watch_out: The polling loop has no time limit, so a job that never finishes keeps the page waiting.

sections.name: App
sections.title: Choosing saved or new analysis
sections.what: Reads the web address to decide whether to show a saved analysis, an error for a bad saved link, or the upload screen. It also reacts when the address changes.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a saved analysis be reopened by a shared link.
sections.watch_out: Saved links are ignored in offline mode, so offline files always open the upload path.

summary: The main screen of the front end: it moves the user from upload to project choice to the programme and 3D views, and holds the helpers that format dates, labels and downloads.
purpose: Brings together the upload, project choice, programme, 3D view, workspace panels and saved views into one application.
why: Likely reason: one root component keeps the flow between screens in a single place.
how: Imports the screens and helpers. Holds small helpers for dates, phase names, file downloads and spreadsheet-safe values. Then defines the project choice screen, the programme and 3D views, and the saved view, and wires them together in the root component.
inputs: Upload reports, project data, activity stories, timeline settings and user actions such as choosing a project or changing a view.
outputs: The rendered screens, downloaded files, and calls to the backend for scenes, jobs and timeline pages.
risks: The file is very large and mixes many screens, so a change in one place can affect another. Date and phase helpers are used across screens, so changing them changes many views.
debug: If a screen is blank, check the state that decides which screen is shown. If a label looks wrong, check the phase label table. If a download fails, check the browser's download setting. Use the browser console for errors from the backend calls.
